question: Explain the arithmetic mean, median and mode as measures of central tendency. State one merit and one limitation of each.

points.label: Arithmetic mean
points.description: The sum of all observations divided by the number of observations.

points.label: Mean: merit and limitation
points.description: Merit: rigidly defined and based on all observations. Limitation: unduly affected by extreme values.

points.label: Median
points.description: The middle value when observations are arranged in ascending or descending order.

points.label: Median: merit and limitation
points.description: Merit: not affected by extreme values and usable with open-end classes. Limitation: not based on all observations and not suited to further algebraic treatment.

points.label: Mode
points.description: The value that occurs most frequently in a set of observations.

points.label: Mode: merit and limitation
points.description: Merit: easy to understand and not affected by extreme values. Limitation: may be ill-defined, or there may be more than one mode.
